review: S10 independent ordering and data review

focusedRun.environment: Windows x64; DOCULIGHT_R3_NODE_ROOT points to the existing Node snapshot

verified: A to B to C and active D retain the latest durable desired content hash and owner-assigned revision; duplicate intent replay does not increment revision.

New-schema equal-millisecond saves, clock rollback, concurrent publication and concurrent ACCEPT use a durable publication-order witness rather than wall-clock or lexical ordering. The gate spans witness reservation, private intent persistence and final-file publication.

Cross-process contention waits asynchronously and publishes in actual order without a caller re-save; stale older-intent replay cannot replace newer final bytes. A to B to A gets a fresh intent identity.

Startup replay automatically converges retained same-body intents after restart and retries a transient real SQLite commit failure without a caller re-save, one intent per event-loop turn with bounded backoff.

Stable document identity, one-to-many original aliases, scalar category, merged tags, existing metadata and path history are preserved; published Markdown and completed imports are not rolled back on indexing failure or cancellation.

Current desired state is enumerated by document-ID keyset across more than one page. A document has at most one active indexing job; active D remains dirty and keyword_dirty, and failed or cancelled history is not reused as the pending winner.
The owner remains the sole authoritative source-ledger and keyword database writer; queued acknowledgement follows the durable metadata and job transaction.

residuals.description: A crashed lock owner's PID could be reused by another live process, leaving the gate conservatively busy until inspection or a later recovery mechanism. PID existence alone cannot safely distinguish the new process from a paused live publisher; age-based theft could corrupt publication order. Already-published private intents can still replay on owner restart.

Pre-witness legacy intents with the same body and millisecond timestamp have no recoverable ordering fact. They remain fail-closed with final bytes and provenance intact instead of inventing a latest scalar metadata winner. The public save producer has not emitted this private schema before issue #37.

scopeBoundary: S11 owns completion-race execution, S12 owns keyword-cache application, and issue #37 owns public save-producer wiring. This review does not claim those outcomes.
